```{=html}
<div class="hp-title">SkillOpt: Executive Strategy for<br>Self-Evolving Agent Skills</div>
<div class="hp-date">May 2026</div>
<div class="hp-authors">
  Yifan Yang<sup>1,*,‡</sup> &nbsp; Ziyang Gong<sup>2,*</sup> &nbsp; Weiquan Huang<sup>3,*</sup> &nbsp; Qihao Yang<sup>2,*</sup> &nbsp; Ziwei Zhou<sup>4,*</sup> &nbsp;
  Zisu Huang<sup>4,*</sup> &nbsp; Yan Li<sup>2</sup> &nbsp; Xuemei Gao<sup>1</sup> &nbsp; Qi Dai<sup>1</sup> &nbsp; Bei Liu<sup>1</sup> &nbsp;
  Kai Qiu<sup>1</sup> &nbsp; Yuqing Yang<sup>1</sup> &nbsp; Dongdong Chen<sup>1</sup> &nbsp; Xue Yang<sup>2,‡</sup> &nbsp; Chong Luo<sup>1</sup>
</div>
<div class="hp-affiliations">
  <sup>1</sup>Microsoft &nbsp; <sup>2</sup>Shanghai Jiao Tong University &nbsp; <sup>3</sup>Tongji University &nbsp; <sup>4</sup>Fudan University
</div>
<div class="hp-abstract">
Agent skills today are hand-crafted, generated one-shot, or evolved through loosely controlled self-revision---none of which behaves like a deep-learning optimizer for the skill, and none of which reliably improves over its starting point under feedback. We argue the skill should instead be <em>trained</em> as the external state of a frozen agent, with the same discipline that makes weight-space optimization reproducible. SkillOpt is, to our knowledge, the first systematic <em>controllable</em> text-space optimizer for agent skills: a separate optimizer model turns scored rollouts into bounded add/delete/replace edits on a single skill document, and an edit is accepted only when it strictly improves a held-out validation score. A textual learning-rate budget, rejected-edit buffer, and epoch-wise slow/meta update make skill training stable while adding zero inference-time model calls at deployment. Across six benchmarks, seven target models, and three execution harnesses (direct chat, Codex, Claude Code), SkillOpt is best or tied on <strong>all 52 evaluated (model, benchmark, harness) cells</strong> and beats every per-cell competitor among human, one-shot LLM, Trace2Skill, TextGrad, GEPA, and EvoSkill skills. On GPT--5.5 it lifts the average no-skill accuracy by <strong>+23.5</strong> points in direct chat, by <strong>+24.8</strong> inside the Codex agentic loop, and by <strong>+19.1</strong> inside Claude Code. Transfer experiments further show that optimized skill artifacts retain value when moved across model scales, between Codex and Claude Code execution environments, and to a nearby math benchmark without further optimization.
</div>
```
